# 4 Ezra Chapter 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Latin Vulgate (Codex Sangermanensis) | **Section:** Core apocalypse — First dialogue

---

**1** Thirty years after Jerusalem fell, I — Salathiel, the one also called Ezra — was living in Babylon. I was lying on my bed, unable to sleep, churning thoughts keeping me awake,

**2** tormented by the sight of Zion's ruins while Babylon's people lived in luxury.

**3** My spirit was in turmoil. I broke out in anguished words before the Most High.

**4** I said: O LORD — you who inhabit eternity, whose eyes are lifted high and whose throne room is above the clouds,

**5** whose reign is beyond all measure, whose glory no mind can take in, before whom the armies of angels stand shaking —

**6** whose attendants are wind and fire, whose every word is true and every promise unbreakable, whose decrees are mighty and whose commands inspire terror,

**7** whose gaze alone drains the ocean depths, whose anger melts the mountains, whose faithfulness never ends —

**8** Hear me, LORD. Hear your servant's prayer. Listen to your creature's plea. Pay attention to what I am saying.

**9** As long as I have breath I will speak. As long as I can think I will question.

**10** Don't focus on the sins of your people — look at those who truly served you.

**11** Don't dwell on the schemes of the wicked — look at those who kept your covenant even while suffering.

**12** Don't call to mind those who walked in evil before you — remember instead those who chose, freely, to fear you.

**13** Please don't set out to destroy those who lived no better than animals; look at those who taught your law faithfully.

**14** Don't vent your anger on those who seem beneath contempt — instead, love those who have always counted on your justice and your glory.

**15** We and our ancestors have lived lives that lead nowhere but death. Yet because of us sinners, you are called merciful.

**16** For if you choose to show mercy to people with no righteous deeds to their name — that is when you truly earn the name Merciful.

**17** The righteous, after all, have their own works stored up with you and will be rewarded accordingly.

**18** But honestly — what is a human being, that you get angry with them? What is this fragile dying race, that you hold a grudge against it?

**19** The truth is, no one born into this world has been without sin. No one who ever lived has been entirely without fault.

**20** And that is exactly where your justice and goodness show up, LORD — in your mercy toward people who have no good works to offer.

**21** And so I pushed further and said: You started this — you spoke, and from nothing you shaped the earth itself and commanded the dust to take form.

**22** Adam obeyed. You breathed life into him; he was yours, made by your own hands. The breath of life came from you, and he stood alive in your presence.

**23** You walked him into paradise — the garden your own right hand had planted before the earth itself existed.

**24** You gave him one rule to keep. He broke it. And right then you decreed death for him and for every generation after him. From him all nations, all peoples, all clans descended — a number impossible to count.

**25** Each nation went its own way. Each one acted wickedly before you and trampled your commands underfoot. And you let them.

**26** Then came your moment — and you sent the flood to wipe out everyone living on earth.

**27** It was the same ending for all of them. Death had claimed Adam; the flood claimed them.

**28** But you saved one — Noah, with his family — the righteous line that came through him.

**29** When the earth's population grew again — children, nations, whole peoples multiplying — they started right back in with their wickedness, worse than those before them.

**30** And while they sinned before you, you singled out one man among them. His name was Abraham.

**31** You loved him. And to him alone — in secret, in the night — you revealed when everything would end.

**32** You cut an everlasting covenant with him and swore you would never abandon his descendants.

**33** You gave him Isaac. Through Isaac came Jacob and Esau. Jacob you kept for yourself; Esau you turned away. And Jacob grew into a great nation.

**34** When you finally led his descendants out of Egypt, you brought them to the foot of Mount Sinai.

**35** You bent the sky down. You rattled the earth. You shook the whole created order, stirred the ocean depths, and sent terror through everything that existed.

**36** Your glory swept through four gates — fire, earthquake, wind, and ice — in order to give your law to Jacob's descendants and your commandments to the people of Israel.
